correctness.rationale: For all origin-containing ellipsoids, affine geometry yields the exact section area \(\pi\sqrt{\det A}\,q^{-3/2}[u^\top(A-cc^\top)u+2t(c\cdot u)-t^2]\). The nonzero prefactor preserves coefficient rank and three offsets invert the Vandermonde matrix. Even/odd parity and constancy of a quadratic form on the sphere give the complete 1/2/3 classification; the exceptional SPD rank-one update has a Euclidean focus at origin. Fish–Ryabogin–Sun–Yaskin 2026 Theorem 4.2 excludes all nonellipsoid finite-rank bodies. Five exact witness ranks and 180 separately computed planar areas passed; neither numerical tests nor source theorem are misrepresented as an independent proof.

originality.rationale: The full primary Fish–Ryabogin–Sun–Yaskin text (arXiv:2610.10229, §§1 and 4, Theorem 4.2) establishes finite separability iff ellipsoidal geometry in the odd-dimensional direction used here; it does not distinguish minimum ranks or isolate a focal off-center exception. Yaskin–Zawalski (arXiv:2306.17127, intro and theorem) concerns origin-symmetric isotropic volumes, while Agranovsky (arXiv:2409.19373, Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.3) treats algebraic section functions and gives a centered formula. A complete coefficient-space argument supplies an additional classification not implied as a stated theorem by those results. Accessible searches and mathematical result records found no equivalent, though possible unindexed classical overlap remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed classical finite-rank Radon-transform treatment may already identify the displaced focal rank-two class.
The infinite-rank conclusion depends on the validity of the cited 2026 Theorem 4.2; the finite ellipsoid rank classification itself is elementary and self-contained.

value.rationale: Minimum separability rank quantifies the exact number of normal-dependent factors necessary to encode all local parallel-section areas, a natural functional invariant in geometric tomography. Its complete classification for every convex spatial body supplements the recent binary ellipsoid rigidity theorem; unexpectedly, a noncentered prolate spheroid retains rank two precisely when the reference origin is a focus. The result explains every finite-rank drop and exhibits every stratum, a structural rather than ad hoc arithmetic classification.
